game.name: Returnal™
game.short_description: BREAK THE CYCLE Fight to survive as this award-winning third-person shooter brings Selene’s story to PC. Take on roguelike challenges. Engage enemies in bullet hell-fuelled clashes. Share your journey through Returnal™ with another player.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 3 (2025)
commentary.summary: Returnal is a third-person shooter action roguelike, billed as the first AAA roguelike, where a big-budget studio adapted the indie-dominated subgenre. He loves the story, atmosphere, biomes, bosses and Metroidvania-style traversal unlocks, and he finished the whole game and enjoyed it. His main frustration is that the roguelike elements (relics, abilities) are dull and make runs feel too similar, which leaves replayability weak. He frames the game as one he likes and wants to be better, and places it on the board with only a vague location cue rather than a tier letter.
praise: Story and first-person segments are captivating
Big budget gives massive, immersive biomes and great visuals
Metroidvania feel: new traversal tools (e.g. sword) unlock across runs
Core third-person gameplay is super enjoyable
Exploration and moving between worlds, especially the first time
criticism: Roguelike elements are disappointing; studio seems not to be a roguelike developer
Relics are boring (more health, more damage, simple triggers)
Runs do not feel different enough from one another
Replayability is weak once the story is finished
The more roguelike mode (the tower) is enjoyable but should be in the core game
unique_points: First AAA-budget roguelike, bringing narrative and world scale to the genre
Plays like a non-roguelike adventure with Metroidvania progression
Design lesson: relics and abilities should subtly change gameplay to differentiate runs without straying from core gameplay
commentary.quote: Even though I spent most of my time complaining about the game, it's just because I like it
design_criteria: Roguelike elements: relic and ability quality and variety are his main complaint
Run variety: runs feel too similar
Replayability: weak after completing the story
Story and narrative: a major strength
Visuals and world immersion: beautiful biomes, big budget polish
Core gameplay feel: third-person shooting is very enjoyable
Meta-progression: Metroidvania traversal unlocks across runs
commentary.rerank_note: He discussed it in his top 10 list of the previous year, so he keeps detail short here.

commentary.label: Top 10 of 2024 (#8)
commentary.summary: Returnal is a third-person action shooter roguelite with metroidvania and horror elements, and one of the first big-budget non-indie roguelites. He thinks the core gameplay, presentation, story and bosses are excellent, but that the roguelite systems are disappointing. He has mixed feelings and regrets not being able to place it higher. It still lands at number 8 and remains one of his favorite roguelites he played this year.
praise: Looks great, with huge, detailed biomes and an immersive world
Grand-adventure campaign feel that indie games rarely match
Story full of mysteries and twists that holds attention
Crisp, satisfying controls with great sound design and visual effects
Solid movement, including the grappling hook for high-speed mobility
criticism: Most artifacts/parasites are simple number tweaks with no unique mechanical changes
Consumables are interesting but situational and not impactful enough to use over the weapon
Weapons drop constantly but with one weapon slot and no recycling they feel unnecessary
Chests are underwhelming, keys are hard to find, and the malignant mechanic is rarely worth the risk
Huge maps can be slow to traverse and sometimes feel like a chore
Runs do not feel different enough from one another
unique_points: One of the first non-independent roguelites, with AAA-scale production and campaign feel
Blends roguelite structure with metroidvania and horror elements
He thinks many consumable effects should have been artifacts instead
commentary.quote: it's sad that I can't put it higher on my list
comparisons: The best roguelites (as inspiration for a sequel)
design_criteria: Core gameplay feel: crisp controls, sound and visual effects
Movement and mobility: grappling hook and high speed
Story and atmosphere: mysteries, twists, creepy horror
Item/artifact design: number tweaks vs unique mechanical changes
Consumable impact: situational, not worth using over the weapon
Weapon system: one slot with no recycling makes drops unnecessary
Risk vs reward: malignant mechanic rarely worth it
Map/level size: good for immersion but tedious to traverse
Run variety: runs feel too similar

community.one_liner: A third-person sci-fi bullet-hell shooter by Housemarque in which astronaut Selene relives death on the alien planet Atropos, with a roguelike run structure, Metroidvania-style traversal unlocks and a cosmic-horror time-loop story.
community.consensus_summary: Critics received Returnal very well: Metacritic is 86 on both PS5 (115 reviews) and PC (Climax Studios port, Feb 2023), and it won Best Game at the British Academy Games Awards. Players are more split: Metacritic user score is 7.4 (68% positive, 12% mixed, 20% negative), and Steam sits at Very Positive (about 81%, roughly 11,100 reviews). Nearly everyone loves the gunplay, movement, sound and atmosphere; the split comes from the brutal difficulty, long runs with thin meta-progression, and (on PC) technical problems. Sony has effectively finished updating it, so PC issues that appeared after the last patch are still open. The game is fully released, not early access.
best_things: Fluid, responsive third-person shooting and movement (dash, jump, melee, adrenaline mechanic) that feels arcade-tight and addictive
Bullet-hell enemy and boss design that is readable and rewards pattern mastery; players talk about getting noticeably better over time
Best-in-class sound design, music and lighting; the oppressive, eerie alien atmosphere (Giger/Beksinski-style visuals) is widely praised
Strong voice performance by Jane Perry and a mysterious psychological-sci-fi story that rewards digging into scout logs and secret endings
Weapon traits, parasites and artifacts create risk/reward decisions inside a run; Metroidvania-style tool unlocks open up traversal
Post-launch content: Ascension update added online co-op and the Tower of Sisyphus endless mode, praised by fans who want pure gameplay with no story
Runs acceptably on modest PCs and supports suspend-cycle saves since Update 2.0, making long runs less punishing
High feel of mastery: many Steam reviewers with 50-180+ hours call it a favourite game of the decade and a Hades alternative for action fans
worst_things: PC port stability: widely reported VRAM/memory leak and texture-streaming degradation after a late patch, forcing restarts every hour or two and never fixed
Crashes on launch or after the logos, black screens and poor frametimes for some players despite high fps
Unwanted Epic Online Services install and optional PlayStation account linking (with region-locked prompts) on Steam drew a wave of negative reviews
Co-op is buggy: lost runs after disconnect as guest, locked shops, reticle/ammo UI bugs, curses carrying over, loading-screen joins, and story progress only counting for the host
Very punishing difficulty with no accessibility or easier mode; a single early hit can cripple a run because healing only raises max health when already full
Environments are repetitive across biomes (same structures, palette swaps) and the loop feels samey after many runs
Sony effectively abandoned PC support; full price on PC years later is criticised, and the next Housemarque game (Saros) is not coming to PC
improvements: Add an easier or accessibility/narrative difficulty so story-focused players can progress
Stronger permanent meta-progression so failed runs feel like they move the needle
Fix the PC VRAM leak and crash bugs and keep patching the port
More build variety: larger pool of weapons, artifacts and non-stat-boost upgrades, plus more biome/environment variety
Shorter runs or more checkpoints beyond suspend-cycle for players with limited time
Fix co-op reliability (reconnect handling, shared story progress) and drop the forced extra launcher/online services
unique_things: Third-person bullet-hell shooter hybrid, rare in a genre dominated by top-down/2D roguelikes
Runs are long (often 1-3 hours) and open-ended with persistent tools and Metroidvania-style gating rather than short quick runs
Procedurally shuffled rooms paired with hand-built biome bosses and handcrafted story progression
Haptic/adaptive trigger and 3D audio design built around the DualSense, carried into a cosmic-horror time-loop narrative
Adrenaline, overload and malfunction systems (parasites, cursed items, weapon proficiency that persists) make every pickup a risk decision
Tower of Sisyphus endless mode and 2-player online co-op added after launch
tedious_or_disliked: Losing a long run to a single mistake, with minimal carry-over; runs feel like they do not respect player time
Having to replay early biomes repeatedly to reach where you died, seeing the same sequences dozens of times
Random trap rooms, laser-heavy rooms and spikes felt cheap or cause lag on some PCs
Incoming attacks are hard to track in chaotic fights, making hits feel unavoidable to some
Needing to restart the PC game every hour because of the memory leak
Unlocks and permanent progression feel too minor to help performance, so the grind feels unrewarding (a top-voted negative review)
divisive_points: Permadeath and no-checkpoint structure: fans see it as thematically perfect and the source of mastery, detractors call it exhausting and unfair
Story: some love the ambiguity and secret endings, others cannot follow it or find the heroine sparsely written
Roguelike credentials: judged as a roguelike, some say it lacks build variety and quick runs; others say it reinvents the genre
PC port: some report flawless performance on cheap hardware, others unplayable instability or VRAM leaks
community.reception_notes: PS5 launch (Apr 2021) was critically acclaimed, with debate over the no-save design; Update 2.0 (Oct 2021) added suspend cycle saves, and the free Ascension update (Mar 2022) added co-op and the Tower of Sisyphus. It sold about 866,000 copies by Feb 2022 and won Best Game at BAFTA. The PC version released Feb 15, 2023 (Climax Studios, PlayStation Publishing) with the same Metacritic 86; many current Steam negatives concern a VRAM leak introduced in a late patch, Epic Online Services and PSN linking, and co-op bugs. Steam data estimates 500k-1M owners and about $10.8M gross / $3.2M net on Steam (Boxleiter-style estimate, not audited). OpenCritic score could not be retrieved (web search budget exhausted, fetches failed), so left null. No first-hand Reddit or IGN pages were readable.
